text: {"standards":[{"code":"W.6.2.c","verdict":"taught","reason":"In the Literacy Lab, students label transitions in the mentor sentences, and in Part B the paragraph requires at least three different transitions, so students practice connecting ideas."},{"code":"W.6.2.d","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Literacy Lab has students circle precise words and expand sentences with adverbials, and Part B requires precise language and vocabulary such as transform and sacrifice to explain the topic."},{"code":"W.6.2.e","verdict":"taught","reason":"The Literacy Lab names formal-style features (no slang, contractions, or 'you'), and Part B requires students to write a paragraph in a formal style that they check against a checklist."},{"code":"W.6.9","verdict":"taught","reason":"In Learning in Action Part A, students record evidence from Chapter 4 and the Raven tale in a chart and then use that evidence in the Part B comparative paragraph."}],"anchorText":{"verdict":"partly","reason":"The Lesson uses The Lightning Thief Chapter 4, pp. 51–56, as the Outline requires, but it leaves the Raven tale unspecified as 'teacher-selected' rather than naming the Judson Raven story the Outline calls for."}}
